sequential.scope: The four named local Eva assertions in the exact C2 fixture and no other sequential property.
limitations: No end-to-end exactly-once, callback, termination or arbitrary-C claim follows.

mutex_protected_concurrency.scope: Only protection of modeled_done in the token-identical Linux sleepable-once helpers, with two paired process-context entries on the pinned UP profile.
limitations: No other Linux mutex user, IRQ/NMI caller, SMP execution, lock implementation proof or unlocked state is covered.

two_process_context_entries.semantics: The main and one discovered Mthread entry independently execute the same paired slow-path caller, with shared-write interference iterated to a fixpoint.
two_process_context_entries.conservative_argument: For the selected two-caller safety property, arbitrary cross-entry interference includes the relevant CONFIG_SMP=n task-preemption orderings; creation success is checked and no completion or join fact is consumed.
limitations: This is an analysis entry enumeration, not a model of a particular kernel task-creation API, scheduler fairness, completion or lifetime handoff.

linux_once_mutex.semantics: A successful Frama_C_mutex_lock acquisition and matching unlock represent exclusive ownership of the configured Linux once_mutex between process-context callers.
linux_once_mutex.conservative_argument: The configured Linux mutex contract admits at most one task owner. Mthread analyzes both task entries with arbitrary shared-write interference, while the fixture initializes one abstract lock before either entry and routes every selected done access through it. For data-race protection of done only, this admits at least the relevant CONFIG_SMP=n task-preemption schedules; blocking, fairness, progress and memory ordering are excluded.
limitations: The kernel mutex implementation itself is source-reviewed and configured-compiled, not proved from its atomic owner field.
No IRQ, softirq, NMI, inter-CPU, weak-memory, lock-free, deadlock, progress or termination claim is made.
The static-key operation and callback side effects are outside the selected property.

static_key_abstraction.semantics: The model records a monitored event but always permits another slow-path attempt.
static_key_abstraction.conservative_argument: For done-access protection, retaining later slow-path attempts overapproximates the real key disabling those attempts; each added attempt still traverses the selected mutex-protected done check.
limitations: No static-branch state, patching, ordering or performance property is checked.

context.ordinary_tasks: two process-context entries with arbitrary Mthread interference
context.preemption: CONFIG_PREEMPT_LAZY=y task interleavings are included abstractly; exact scheduler points and liveness are not modeled
context.interrupts: excluded because Linux mutex_lock/mutex_unlock are forbidden in hardware and software interrupt contexts
context.lifetime: once_mutex, done, key and harness module objects are static and remain live for both entries

property.claim: In the token-identical __do_once_sleepable_start/done bodies, two correctly paired process-context slow-path callers access their shared done flag only while the same configured Linux mutex abstraction is held.
exclusions: End-to-end exactly-once callback execution is not an automated result.
Callback data, failures and side effects are not modeled.
The static-key fast path and static_branch_disable semantics are not verified.
Actual subsystem call sites outside the DO_ONCE_SLEEPABLE pairing contract are not verified.
Interrupt, NMI, SMP, weak-memory, atomic, RCU and lock-free behavior is not verified.
Deadlock freedom, fairness, progress, termination and post-join final state are not verified.
